testing: report test discovery states and empty runs

Report the known discovery state when VS Code cannot select or execute tests.
Do not present an empty test run as a successful validation.

- Distinguish missing files, unavailable discovery, pending discovery, and provider errors.
- Bound discovery waits and release listeners on cancellation.
- Preserve discovery failures without replacing provider-supplied errors.
- Report unmatched files and test names in partial requests.
- Skip empty workspace controllers and report zero-execution runs as unvalidated.
- Keep normal test results and coverage reports unchanged.
- Add regression tests and update the unit-test guidance.

Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog/issues/9126

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed line unconditionally reads each task's full output and converts all buffers to strings whenever no test reaches passed, failed, or errored. Output length is explicitly unbounded here; only the frequency and real-world log sizes are uncertain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: output bytes, VSBuffer slices, JavaScript strings, and serialized tool-result content
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Allocation and copy cost is O(total output bytes across all tasks), with additional joined-string allocation; there is no upper bound before materialization.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: memory/GC pressure and increased tool-response serialization latency
Findings.PreviousBehavior: A zero-execution result flowed through the normal summary path, which did not read task output when there were no failed/errored tests.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new zero-execution branch calls `getRange(0, task.output.length).toString()` for every task and joins all complete outputs into the returned tool content.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 242 newly reads and stringifies complete task outputs; the deleted implementation did not include task output in an empty result.
Findings.Title: Bound empty-run output before materializing it
Findings.Impact: A runner that emits a large compile, discovery, or import log but executes no tests causes the extension host/workbench to copy the entire log into strings and then into one more joined result, creating CPU/GC pressure, retained response bytes, and potentially a very large chat-tool payload.
Findings.Evidence: RIGHT line 242 has no byte, line, or token cap and scales directly with every task's full `output.length`. The branch is specifically reached for zero-execution failures, where verbose build/import diagnostics are a realistic trigger; the added tests exercise this path with runner output.
Findings.Recommendation: Apply a shared total byte/character budget before reading buffers (for example, bounded head/tail excerpts per task with a global cap) and append a truncation marker, so useful diagnostics remain without materializing unbounded output.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed call path is explicit: every requested URI starts IFileService.stat, and the enclosing Promise.all must settle before test selection and runTests. The added tests themselves establish that one stalled stat makes an otherwise runnable request take the full 5,000 ms deadline; only the prevalence of slow providers is uncertain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: filesystem/provider I/O calls, potentially remote IPC/network operations
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Boundary cardinality is one concurrent stat per requested file; critical-path latency is governed by the slowest check and reaches the fixed 5,000 ms deadline for any stalled path.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: blocked test-start latency and unnecessary remote I/O
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Explicit-file invocations mapped paths to URIs and queried the in-memory test collection via testsInFile; they did not issue filesystem/provider stats before starting matching tests.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The diff starts one IFileService.stat per requested file and awaits all checks together with discovery before invoking runTests.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 478 newly invokes `this._fileService.stat(file.uri)` for every explicit file; no corresponding boundary existed in the deleted `_getFileTestsToRun` implementation.
Findings.Title: Keep file-stat diagnostics off the test-run critical path
Findings.Impact: In remote or virtual workspaces, one slow or stalled provider stat delays every already-discovered matching test by up to the shared five-second deadline; a request for F files also creates F concurrent filesystem/provider calls.
Findings.Evidence: The added `await raceCancellationError(this._fileService.stat(file.uri), discoveryToken.token)` is included in `checks`, and line 491 awaits `Promise.all([...checks, ...selection])`. The new `runs a known healthy file despite a stalled stat` test asserts exactly 5,000 ms elapsed even though `/workspace/a.ts` is already discovered and then runs successfully.
Findings.Recommendation: Use in-memory discovery to start known matches immediately. Run existence checks only for unmatched paths or in parallel for later diagnostics without awaiting them before `runTests`, while retaining cancellation and bounded diagnostic completion.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The before/after is direct in the diff: the old no-files branch returned collection roots immediately, while the new branch awaits expansion and idle state for every root. Tests confirm a stalled controller holds a healthy controller for the full five-second deadline. Provider-specific discovery cost varies, which affects magnitude but not the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: extension-host/controller discovery IPC, provider CPU/I/O, and published test-item allocations
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Work grows with the number of registered roots and each provider's discovery tree; concurrency is unbounded across roots, while critical-path latency is the slowest root up to the shared five-second timeout.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased test-start latency, provider work, and allocation pressure
Findings.PreviousBehavior: With no `files` argument, `_getFileTestsToRun` immediately returned the published root items; with no name filter those roots were passed directly to `runTests`, allowing providers to execute without pre-enumerating their trees.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The no-files path now concurrently expands every expandable controller root, waits for discovery to become idle, and only selects roots that published children before it starts the run.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 535 adds an awaited root expansion on the no-files path; the deleted code returned `collection.rootItems` without expansion.
Findings.Title: Preserve lazy selection for unfiltered workspace runs
Findings.Impact: A normal all-workspace test request now eagerly invokes every controller's discovery work and can wait five seconds for one stalled controller before any healthy tests start; large providers may also enumerate and publish substantial test trees solely to begin an all-tests run.
Findings.Evidence: RIGHT line 535 awaits `_expandRoot` inside `Promise.all` over all root items, followed by `_waitForDiscovery`. The new `preserves ready workspace controller selection` test asserts 5,000 ms elapsed when one of two controllers stalls, despite the healthy controller being runnable.
Findings.Recommendation: For unfiltered all-workspace requests, keep passing roots directly to `runTests` and use the new zero-executed-result handling to classify empty runs. Restrict eager discovery to requests that require enumeration, such as name filtering or unresolved explicit files.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The loops and call count are explicit: for each explicit file, this method traverses the full collection and runs `file.tests.some` for unrelated items, and invoke calls it both before and after the run. The repository already documents large per-file test collections as a performance-sensitive case; exact collection sizes per user remain the only magnitude uncertainty.
Findings.PerformanceResource: CPU string-prefix comparisons and temporary traversal/allocation work
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For F requested files the added work is O(sum over files of N×T_file), plus repeated O(N) collection traversals; it runs once during discovery and again after execution.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: CPU pressure and increased pre-run/post-run response latency
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The old explicit-file path used the URI index through `testsInFile` and did not rescan the entire workspace collection to construct discovery diagnostics.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: For every requested file, `_updateDiscoveryEvidence` walks every collection item and, for items not matched by URI or the ancestor set, linearly searches all tests already matched to that file. The method is then repeated after the test run.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 580 introduces the nested `file.tests.some` within the newly added full-collection loop; both invocations of `_updateDiscoveryEvidence` are also added by this diff.
Findings.Title: Avoid cross-product scans when collecting file diagnostics
Findings.Impact: In a monorepo with N discovered tests and T top-level tests in a requested file, diagnostics can perform roughly N×T prefix checks per file, twice per invocation, delaying the tool response and consuming CPU even when the tests themselves are ready.
Findings.Evidence: RIGHT line 580 uses `file.tests.some(test => TestId.isChild(...))` inside `for (const item of collection.all)`. Call sites are lines 523 and 231. The surrounding `testsInFile` code explicitly notes that large numbers of tests in one file previously caused long delays (#235819), establishing this as a realistic collection shape.
Findings.Recommendation: Build the relevant set by traversing descendants from the file-matched nodes (and adding ancestors once), or use a prefix tree/index, then do O(1) membership checks during at most one collection pass. Recompute only evidence that can actually change after the run.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run tests for one or more explicit files, including remote/virtual workspace files
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The tool canonicalizes every path, then awaits one combined Promise.all containing all file stats and all file-discovery tasks; only after every member settles does it call runTests. Thus path checks are on the critical path even when the in-memory URI index already has a runnable match.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: IFileService.stat for every requested URI, potentially crossing remote/virtual filesystem providers
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per supplied path, including duplicates; F calls launch together.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Explicit-file selection used testsInFile and the in-memory URI index without statting each path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Promise.all waits for the slowest call, up to the shared five-second deadline, before any matched test run starts.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Expand relevant controller roots/test items through the main-thread test collection into test providers
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one root expansion per distinct root per invocation after coalescing, plus URI-directed item expansion in testsInFile.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old file path relied on testsInFile and did not proactively expand every eligible URI-less root when no item was indexed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Expansion is awaited before selection; the shared timeout bounds it to five seconds.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start the selected test run through ITestService.runTests
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical run request after deduplicating selected test IDs; internal provider grouping remains unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same logical run boundary existed before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This is the intended execution boundary after discovery.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: F requested paths, N tests in the workspace collection, and T_file top-level matched tests for each file. Stats have effective cardinality F; diagnostic evidence costs O(sum(N*T_file)).
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All F stats and F file-selection tasks launch concurrently without a limiter. Root expansions are coalesced per root within the invocation by rootExpansions and also use MainThreadTestCollection's per-item expansion promise; the slowest stat/discovery task gates the batch.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The collection has a warm URI index and expansion-level promise cache, and rootExpansions coalesces roots within one invocation. The newly added file stats have no tool-level positive/negative cache, so even warm known matches issue a fresh stat. Discovery cancellation after five seconds prevents indefinite waiting but does not remove the delay.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: boundary placement, full-collection loops, nested matched-test search, coalescing, and deadline behavior are directly visible in changed code and tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Remote provider stat duration and real F/N/T_file vary, but a new test fixes the stalled-stat delay at exactly five seconds and repository comments establish large per-file collections as realistic.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable regressions: fresh per-file stats gate known matches, and per-file diagnostics perform repeated collection-by-file-test cross-product scans.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run all workspace tests with no file or name filters
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The old path selected root items immediately. The changed path expands every expandable/busy root and waits for every root to become idle in one Promise.all before runTests can begin.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request lazy discovery for each controller root
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to C concurrent root expansions, one per published root after per-root coalescing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No-file/no-name requests returned rootItems directly and did not pre-enumerate provider trees.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All must finish or hit the shared timeout before healthy roots are passed to runTests.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical run request after discovery.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This run began immediately after root selection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Starts only after the new all-root discovery barrier.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: C registered/published controller roots and the amount of provider discovery work/test items each root publishes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All root discovery requests launch concurrently with no global limiter; completion is a barrier across all roots. MainThreadTestCollection coalesces expansion per root, but one stalled root holds the whole selection until the shared five-second cancellation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Already-expanded roots avoid new expansion on warm state. Cold or reset roots invoke providers; per-item expansion promises coalesce duplicate requests, with no cross-root backpressure.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the deleted immediate return and added all-root expansion barrier provide a direct before/after, corroborated by timeout tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider discovery may be cheap when warm, but cold providers can do arbitrary extension-side I/O and tests demonstrate a healthy controller waiting five seconds for a stalled peer.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable eager-work regression: unfiltered all-workspace runs now force and await discovery that was previously unnecessary to start execution.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run tests filtered by test names
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The tool discovers candidate files/roots, recursively waits for and expands nonmatching suites, filters labels, then executes selected items. A single shared five-second token bounds discovery and releases listeners on cancellation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Expand test items to discover descendants needed for name matching
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Potentially one expansion per expandable visited suite, coalesced by the collection; sibling requests are concurrent.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Name filtering already recursively expanded nonmatching suites with Promise.all; the PR changes waiting/cancellation semantics rather than introducing this multiplicity.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required to determine name matches, but bounded by the shared discovery deadline.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of discovered suites/items and requested names; sibling expansions can span the selected tree.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Top-level and child filtering uses Promise.all, so sibling expansions can run concurrently without a global limiter. This recursive concurrency largely existed before; the PR adds cancellation-aware waits and a shared deadline.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Expanded items and MainThreadTestCollection expansion promises are reused. Name matches are recomputed per invocation; no result cache is appropriate because collection state can change.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the call path and concurrency; no distinct diff-caused performance regression beyond the reported explicit-file diagnostics and all-root eager expansion.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Tree widths and provider expansion cost vary.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: recursive name discovery was pre-existing, while the added deadline and listener cleanup bound its lifetime.

Scenarios.Scenario: Capture a completed run and report zero executed tests
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the existing runTests boundary and completion monitoring, the new zero-execution branch collects provider errors and materializes every task's complete output into the returned tool result.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start and capture the live test result
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical run request; result event listeners are disposed on finish/cancellation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The tool already started and monitored one run.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing execution boundary; cancellation cleanup is improved by the diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read each task's entire output buffer, convert to strings, join, and embed in chat tool content
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full-buffer read per task and O(B) copied bytes, followed by an additional joined string.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Zero-test summaries did not read all task output.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs synchronously before the tool can return the zero-execution diagnostic.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total output bytes B across all tasks in a run where passed+failed+errored equals zero.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Output conversion is synchronous and sequential on the response path; there is no limiter or chunking. Result capture still uses one five-second grace timer for taskless runs, comparable to the old timeout behavior.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No output transformation cache; all bytes are copied from task buffers on each invocation. There is no cap before conversion or join.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: full ranges and joined strings are explicit, and branch reachability is covered by added zero-execution tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Most logs are small, but compile/import failures that prevent all test execution can be verbose and no code bound limits B.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable serialization/allocation regression: unbounded runner output is materialized before any truncation.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all nine changed files and every diff page. Four diff-caused issues were submitted: per-file stat gating, eager all-root discovery, repeated cross-product diagnostic scans, and unbounded empty-run output materialization. Cancellation/listener cleanup, expansion coalescing, result capture, and pre-existing name-filter concurrency were also checked.
